title: GIF cut-out gives an already-transparent clip a BLACK background - the mask replaces the frame's alpha
description: Fabio, 2026-09-20: cutting a clip that already has a transparent background comes back with a black one. `applyMaskAlpha` (routes/gifCutout.js) joins the new mask in as the frame's alpha, REPLACING what was there, and flattens the old alpha onto black first - so every pixel the new mask keeps that was already transparent turns opaque and shows the black the flatten just painted. A cut can only ever remove: the frame's own alpha is the ceiling. Half of the additive-masking complaint; the Add/Subtract rework of the mask methods is its own card.
